The spec says: a fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer. When full, the OLDEST value is dropped to make room for the new one, so size never exceeds capacity.

Current bug: `push` on a full buffer just returns the buffer unchanged — it drops the NEW value instead of the OLDEST. Fix: when full, drop the oldest (head) and append the new value.

Minimal fix:

```elixir
def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
  items =
    if length(items) >= capacity do
      tl(items) ++ [value]
    else
      items ++ [value]
    end
  %{buffer | items: items}
end
```

Or minimal edit:

```elixir
def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
  if length(items) >= capacity do
    %{buffer | items: tl(items) ++ [value]}
  else
    %{buffer | items: items ++ [value]}
  end
end
```

That changes as little as possible. Let me apply and test.
content: The bug: `push` on a full buffer drops the *new* value (returns buffer unchanged) instead of dropping the oldest, as the `@moduledoc` specifies.
Fixed `push` to drop the oldest value when full (previously it silently dropped the new value), verified overflow, size, pop, and empty-pop all match the `@moduledoc`.
